Gloucestershire Constabulary official newsroom — Exa metadata: published 2026-09-27. This is the force's own release carrying ACC Richard Ocone's 2pm Sunday statement. Date confirmed from Exa metadata plus the statement's internal wording "today (Sunday 27 September)". SEARCH HIGHLIGHTS.
NOTE: an attempt to fetch the live Gloucestershire Police news index on the morning of 28 Sep 2026 returned CRAWL_INFRASTRUCTURE_ERROR, so NO Monday-morning force update could be confirmed. Latest confirmed force position is Sunday.

ACC Richard Ocone gave the following statement to media this afternoon in relation to the ongoing major incident.

"At around 12.45am today (Sunday 27 September) police received a call relating to three suspicious vehicles travelling towards RAF Fairford.

"Armed officers responded and subsequently arrested five men in the Whelford area on suspicion of committing offences under the Explosives Act.

"Counter Terrorism Policing are now leading the investigation.

"A 400m cordon has been put in place around the vehicles while the Army's Explosive Ordinance Disposal unit examine them.

"As a precaution, around 85 households have been advised to evacuate while these examinations take place.

"Gloucestershire Police's focus at this time is on the local community and I'd like to thank the residents who have left their homes this morning for their understanding and support.

"We appreciate the disruption this will have caused and would like to reassure them we are working as quickly as we can to get them back in their properties."
